newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-VENEZUELA, PUERTO RICO WIN AT CARIBBEAN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-VENEZUELA, PUERTO RICO WIN AT CARIBBEAN SERIES.

text.p: Luis Raven slammed a second-inning home run which set Venezuela on the way to a 7-0 win Wednesday over the Dominican Republic in the Caribbean Baseball Series.
Raven drove his solo home run to left field off Dominican starter and loser Jose Parra. Venezuela picked up two more runs in the third on RBI hits by Edgardo Alfonzo and Richard Hidalgo.

Venezuela, represented by the Magallanes Navigators, scored twice more in the fifth when Raven doubled and scored on a double by Luis Sojo, who played with the Major League Baseball champion New York Yankees last year. Sojo scored on an RBI single by Clemente Alvarez.
Alfonzo homered to centre field in the sixth, with Sojo's RBI single adding the seventh and final run in the same inning.
Ramon Garcia went eight innings for the win for Venezuela, scattering five hits and getting the benefit of four double plays. Parra allowed eight hits and four runs in four and one third innings.
Heavily favoured Puerto Rico had a six-run fourth inning and used 12 hits and two home runs to hold off Mexico 9-8 in the other game Wednesday.

Wil Cordero of the Boston Red Sox had a three-run home run in the fourth and Jose Hernandez also homered for Puerto Rico while Darrel Brinkley and Oscar Romero homered for Mexico, the defending champion represented by the Culican Tomato Growers.
The Dominicans, represented by the Aguilas Cibaenas, also lost to Puerto Rico 7-4 on Tuesday and are in danger of finishing last in the four-nation tournament. Mexico defeated Venezuela Tuesday 3-1.
On Thursday, Venezuela meets Puerto Rico and Mexico plays the Dominican Republic. The double round robin ends Sunday.
